items.title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience. About the Role We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows. This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale. You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees. We’re looking for someone with: - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail. - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows. - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance. - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures. - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination. - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results. - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations. In this role, you will: - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements. - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue. - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues. - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions. - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners. - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability. - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands. - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions. - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements. - Understand how invoices, approvals, supplier records, payment instructions, bank status, settlement, and reconciliation fit together, and can investigate discrepancies across them. - Bring a strong controls mindset aligned to SOX, including practical judgment on bank-detail changes, duplicate prevention, segregation of duties, reconciliation, and close support. - Have designed or improved ERP/AP payment workflows and bank integrations, including host-to-host automation, with tested controls and measurable results. - Have led teams or BPO partners through clear expectations, coaching, capacity planning, and sustained improvements in service and quality. - Communicate clearly with suppliers, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and can resolve issues across teams without losing ownership. - Are willing to work directly in payment queues, investigate failures, and support close when needed. - Experience with Oracle Fusion, Zip, or comparable integrated finance systems, and practical use of AI in controlled finance workflows, would be helpful. You’ll work directly with our agency partners, product teams, data science, and platform reps (Meta, Google, Apple) across regions. If you’re the kind of person who can context-switch between a Meta CAPI payload spec and a creative brief in the same afternoon, this role was made for you.

items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Crawler)
items.description: Keeping a crawler running is not the same as keeping it productive. Queues can grow while servers look healthy, and a small change can become a fleet-wide bottleneck. On Perplexity's Crawler team, you'll improve throughput, plan capacity, and build operational reliability through safer deployments, better observability, and durable fixes. Responsibilities - Operate and optimize Kubernetes workloads and supporting infrastructure for crawler services, including fetching and rendering fleets. - Build and maintain infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines, with safe rollouts, validation, and fast rollback. - Define SLOs and build monitoring, alerting, and observability for availability, latency, throughput, and resource saturation. - Own capacity planning and resource efficiency; diagnose queue backlogs, network failures, and resource bottlenecks with service owners. - Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response, and turn blameless postmortems into durable reliability improvements. - Write production software to automate diagnosis and routine remediation, with validation and approval gates for high-impact actions. Qualifications - 5+ years of experience in SRE, production engineering, or infrastructure-heavy backend roles, with strong programming skills in Python, C++, Rust, or Go. - Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, production Kubernetes, infrastructure as code such as Terraform, and automated deployment workflows. - Strong Linux and networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP, and load balancing. - Experience building observability with tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and using SLOs to guide reliability improvements. - Proven experience diagnosing distributed-system failures, leading production incidents, and improving system performance or resource efficiency. Nice to have - Experience operating web crawlers, search infrastructure, or browser fleets at scale. - Experience with distributed queues, backpressure, workload isolation, or multi-region recovery.

items.title: Program Manager, Local Community Impact
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Community team builds direct relationships with people who use OpenAI’s technology, helps others learn from their experiences, and brings their insights back to product and research teams. Our programs connect communities with trusted partners who help organizations adopt AI effectively. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Program Manager to build and run our partner network. You will turn an early program into a reliable operation: recruit and onboard partners, coordinate agreements and payments, manage external service providers, support local events and marketing, review service quality, and improve the program as we learn. This partner network will be on the ground in communities helping people–from small businesses, non-profits, and community organizations–experience concrete benefits from our technology. They will set up useful workflows, learn OpenAI tools and become more confident, independent users. You should be as comfortable helping a partner resolve an onboarding issue as you are designing the systems that prevent it from happening again. You will work with local operators and internal teams to make sure commitments are clear, work gets done, and the people we serve receive useful, high-quality support. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Build the partner operating model, from sourcing and selection of partners through onboarding, ongoing support, renewal and exit. Establish clear expectations, owners, timelines and escalation paths. Create a scalable operating model that supports program growth and evolving partner needs. - Run partner onboarding with Legal, Finance and Procurement: track agreements, required information, vendor setup, readiness and start dates so partners can begin work and receive payments through approved processes. - Manage partner payments, reporting and related operational processes. - Plan and support local workshops, deployments and events with partners. Coordinate audiences, venues, budgets, materials, staffing and follow-up while preserving local ownership. - Coordinate program marketing and communications with Community, Marketing and content partners. Develop clear partner guidance, route brand and messaging approvals, and help useful stories and practices reach the right audiences. - Build trusted relationships with local operators and the organizations they serve. Coach partners, answer questions, address service-quality concerns and set clear boundaries around access, funding and program participation. - Create practical systems for the partner community: intake, a shared knowledge base, service logs, regular check-ins and reusable playbooks that reduce manual work without sacrificing quality. - Develop and operate partner review processes with the hiring manager and relevant teams. Combine verified service delivery, beneficiary feedback and sustained product use to understand performance and improve support. - Collaborate with analytics and product teams to assess program impact using appropriate data and feedback. - Manage budgets, vendors, risks and dependencies across the program. Keep stakeholders informed, surface decisions early and bring recurring partner feedback into program and product improvements. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - 8+ years owning a complex partner, community or operational program from early design through execution at scale, with clear examples of what you personally built and improved. - Bring strong operational judgment and follow-through across onboarding, financial workflows, events and multiple stakeholder groups. - Can earn trust with small-business owners, local technical operators and community leaders, explain expectations plainly and have difficult conversations when needed. - Have practical familiarity with ChatGPT, Codex and AI-enabled workflows, and can work credibly with technical specialists while explaining tools to people with less technical experience. - Use data and qualitative feedback to distinguish meaningful outcomes from activity counts, and can improve a process without making it unnecessarily bureaucratic. - Write clearly, communicate risks early, work independently through ambiguity and collaborate effectively across teams. - Have experience creating playbooks, support systems or automation that lets a high-touch program scale. NICE TO HAVE - Operating a local-services, small-business, nonprofit, fellowship, ambassador or distributed partner program. - Coordinating vendor onboarding, invoices, budgets or grant-like payment workflows with Finance and Legal. - Running hands-on workshops or community events and translating successful local practices into reusable resources. - Working across marketing, product, analytics and public-policy or regional teams. items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Web Access Engineer, Crawler)
items.description: Perplexity is hiring a Web Access Engineer for the Crawler team to build reliable fetching and rendering systems for AI-powered search. You'll work on freely available public web content, within site permissions and approved access policies, and develop the infrastructure that supplies content to downstream indexing and retrieval systems. Your focus will be diagnosing network errors, page-loading issues, and incomplete rendering. You'll trace problems from network protocols through client-side execution, distinguish technical failures from intentional access restrictions, and turn findings into production fixes that improve content quality and efficiency at scale. Responsibilities - Own fetching and rendering improvements end to end, from investigation through implementation and production rollout, partnering with crawler engineers and SREs. - Investigate fetch and rendering failures across DNS, TLS, HTTP, caching, redirects, and client-side rendering, and classify root causes. - Improve page loading, completion detection, and content capture to preserve relevant content and handle dynamic pages reliably. - Ensure the crawler respects site-imposed access restrictions and rate limits, identifies itself clearly, and retries only transient technical errors. - Build tools to reproduce failures, compare crawler output against expected page content, and turn findings into regression tests. - Define metrics for fetching reliability, content completeness, and error classification, and use them to prioritize improvements. Qualifications - 5+ years of software engineering experience in web infrastructure, browsers, CDNs, or crawling, with strong programming skills in at least one of Go, Python, Rust, or C++. - Deep understanding of HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, including status semantics, caching, conditional requests, content encoding, and redirects; strong knowledge of TLS, DNS, cookies, and sessions. - Understanding of CDN caching and content delivery, HTTP error handling, retry backoff, and server-defined rate limits. - Knowledge of page lifecycle, network idle, service workers, client-side rendering, and shadow DOM; experience debugging JavaScript and fluency with Chrome DevTools, CDP, HAR files, curl, and packet captures. - Comfort working independently when the path forward is not fully defined. Nice to have - Experience developing CDN, caching, or web performance systems. - Experience operating crawlers, headless browsers, or distributed content-acquisition systems at scale. - Contributions to a browser engine or JavaScript runtime.

items.title: Head of Marketing Operations
items.location_text: San Francisco, Austin, New York City
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our enterprise marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. We've grown this far without a marketing automation platform or a dedicated Marketing Operations team. We're ready to build both. We're hiring our first Head of Marketing Operations. You'll choose and implement our first marketing automation platform. You'll own how every marketing and product lead is enriched, scored and routed. And you'll build the campaign operations, attribution and reporting that connect our B2B and enterprise marketing to pipeline and revenue. You'll report to the Head of Revenue Operations and build a team. Your first direct report is a GTM Engineer, who builds our enrichment, scoring and routing systems in code. You set the definitions, strategy and priorities for that work, and the GTM Engineer is your force multiplier for delivering it. Tech stack: Salesforce | Snowflake | dbt | Clay | Marketing automation (you'll choose it) | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Computer WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious. - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it. - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users. - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products. - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build and lead the Marketing Operations team. Manage the GTM Engineer from day one, set the team's roadmap, and hire the next roles as the function grows. Stay hands-on while the team is small. - Select and implement our marketing automation platform. Run the evaluation across established and AI-native platforms, covering requirements, integrations, security, scale and total cost. Then lead the rollout: the data model, the Salesforce sync, lifecycle stages, program templates, permissions and the migration of our existing B2B email programs. - Own the lead lifecycle. Define lifecycle stages, qualification criteria, handoff SLAs and recycle rules with Marketing and Sales leadership. Make sure they are enforced the same way in the marketing automation platform and in Salesforce. - Own enrichment, scoring and routing. You are accountable for every lead being complete, accurately scored on fit, intent and product usage, and sent to nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager within SLA. The GTM Engineer builds and runs these systems. You direct the work, supply marketing engagement signals to the scoring model, and answer to Sales and Marketing for the results. - Own or co-own the prospecting tools our BDRs use. Lead the implementation and evolution of these tools, which will be a combination of internally built applications and vendor solutions. Work with BDR leadership to set requirements, decide what to build and what to buy, drive adoption, and measure the impact on meetings and pipeline. The GTM Engineer delivers the internal builds and the integrations with vendor tools. - Stand up account-based marketing and sales as a motion. Work with Sales and Marketing leadership to select and tier target accounts by fit, intent and product usage, and set the level of investment for each tier, from one-to-one plans for strategic accounts to scaled programs for the broader list. Map the buying group at each account and roll individual engagement up to an account-level score that tells BDRs and AEs when to act. Design the coordinated plays that Marketing, BDRs and AEs run together across email, ads, events and outbound, with clear triggers, owners and follow-up SLAs. Measure the program by account: buying-group coverage, engagement, meetings, pipeline and win rate against comparable non-target accounts. The GTM Engineer builds the account scoring, signals and orchestration behind these plays. - Run nurture and campaign operations for B2B and enterprise marketing. Build the nurture tracks that leads enter when they aren't ready for sales, including entry and exit rules. Set up a repeatable way to build, test and launch email, webinar, event, paid and account-based programs. Keep a clean Salesforce campaign structure so every program rolls up correctly. - Own attribution and marketing reporting. Build the tracking and lead source model, define how we measure pipeline that marketing sourced and influenced, and own the dashboards and weekly funnel review that leadership uses. Marketing and Revenue Operations should report the same numbers. - Protect data quality, consent and deliverability. Own consent, preferences and suppression for B2B and enterprise marketing email under GDPR, CCPA and CAN-SPAM. Own sending-domain health and inbox placement for that email. The Growth team owns product and consumer lifecycle messaging, so agree shared rules with them on contact frequency, suppression and sending domains. - Partner with Growth on web conversion. Growth owns the website, sign-up flows and in-product surfaces. You own what happens to a B2B lead after capture: form field standards, tracking parameters, consent capture, and a clean handoff into the marketing automation platform and Salesforce. - Own the marketing technology stack and its budget. Evaluate vendors, manage renewals, add what the team needs and retire what it has outgrown. - Set the operating rhythm. Run intake and prioritization for marketing operations requests, document every system, and train marketers and sellers on how to use what you build. - Use AI to do more with a small team. Use Computer and other AI tools to automate campaign builds, data cleanup, reporting and lifecycle workflows. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In your first 30 days: - Audit how leads are captured, enriched, scored, routed and emailed today, and document the gaps. - Write the requirements for the marketing automation platform and start the evaluation. - Agree with Growth on who owns which messages, audiences and sending domains. In your first 60 days: - Select the platform and start implementation with a clear rollout plan. - Publish agreed lifecycle stage definitions and handoff SLAs. - Set the GTM Engineer's priorities for enrichment, scoring and routing, and publish a baseline funnel report. In your first 120 days: - Take the platform live with a reliable Salesforce sync, consent and preference management, and the first nurture programs running. - Have scoring and routing meet the agreed speed-to-lead SLA. - Deliver a first attribution model that Marketing, Sales and Finance all use. In your first 6 months: - Build the team beyond the GTM Engineer, based on a hiring plan you've made the case for. - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion. - Report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline as one trusted number in company planning. QUALIFICATIONS - 8+ years in marketing operations or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including 2+ years managing people. - Experience at a company with a large consumer user base alongside an enterprise business, coordinating with a product lifecycle or growth team. - You've led the selection and implementation of a marketing automation platform from scratch, or a full migration, including the Salesforce sync. - Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one major platform, such as HubSpot or Marketo. You can still build in it yourself. - You've designed, shipped and measured a lead scoring and routing model, with a lifecycle and SLAs that Sales followed. - You've built attribution and pipeline reporting that Sales and Finance used to make decisions. - Experience directing technical builders, such as GTM engineers, systems engineers or analysts. You can scope technical work, set priorities and judge the result. - Working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns) and enough SQL to trace a record across systems. - Working knowledge of consent and privacy rules (GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM) and email deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, list hygiene). - Clear communicator. You explain systems and data to executives without jargon, and turn business requests into requirements. - Builder mindset. You're comfortable being the first hire in a function and creating structure where none exists. NICE TO HAVE - Experience in a hybrid product-led and sales-led motion, including product-qualified leads and mapping users to accounts. - Experience with a warehouse-first stack: Snowflake, dbt, reverse ETL and Clay. - Experience deploying AI-native marketing tools or agents in production. - Experience running event and webinar operations, including lead capture and follow-up. - Experience building a marketing operations team from the first hire.

items.title: Senior Software Engineer, Trump Accounts
items.location_text: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. Robinhood has been tapped as the brokerage and initial trustee for Trump Accounts, and is working alongside BNY and The U.S. Department of Treasury to develop and operate the program, which aims to expand market access for the next generation of Americans. In this role, you will help build a world-class, intuitive platform, leveraging Robinhood’s industry-leading financial technology to deliver a standalone web and app experience for this historic national initiative. The Government Products team focuses on building and scaling systems that support long-term investing and account management for millions of customers. This team works closely with product, data, and infrastructure partners to deliver reliable, secure, and intuitive experiences. You will help shape systems that enable customers to plan for their financial future with confidence! As a Senior Software Engineer , you will design and build large-scale distributed systems that support real-time trading, balances, and platform capabilities. You will lead technically complex projects, contribute to architectural decisions, and collaborate with frontend and data partners to deliver well-structured APIs. Your work will directly influence system performance, operational safety, and long-term maintainability across core Robinhood products. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA and New York, NY offices, with hybrid attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Build and evolve scalable backend systems, balancing performance, reliability, and long-term maintainability. Design, implement, test, and release product-facing features with strict correctness and availability requirements. Partner with frontend and data engineers to define and refine REST APIs that serve millions of customers. Lead large, technically complex projects from design through execution. Mentor junior engineers through code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on technical guidance. Identify opportunities to improve system performance, developer productivity, and operational risk. What you bring 5+ years of professional software development experience. 3+ years of experience building low-latency, large-scale distributed systems in production environments. Experience designing and operating highly concurrent systems and well-structured REST APIs. Demonstrated ownership of large projects with sustained impact on a system or team. Strong technical judgment and the ability to prioritize work aligned with business and reliability goals. Ability to break down complex problems and deliver practical, high-quality solutions. Experience mentoring other engineers and contributing to technical direction on new initiatives. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Best in class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Lifestyle wallet — a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces Position Restriction: This position is restricted to US citizens or lawful permanent residents In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $196,000 — $230,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $172,000 — $202,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $153,000 — $179,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Asset Movements Operations team at Robinhood is dedicated to offering fast, safe, and secure execution of customer requests such as wires, checks, and internal account transfers. As a critical pillar of Robinhood's brokerage business model, our team focuses on risk management and operational accuracy to support the firm's growth. We collaborate with Customer Experience, Clearing, Fraud, and Financial Crimes teams to troubleshoot complex issues and ensure seamless processing. Our culture thrives on teamwork, continuous improvement, and a shared dedication to protecting our customers' assets. Together, we are building the future of retail brokerage operations! As an Asset Movements Operations Specialist, you will play a central role in executing daily financial transactions with precision and resolving customer requests. In this position, you will be accountable for high-priority wire, check, and journal processing while identifying operational inefficiencies. You will collaborate with project and operations teams to launch and scale Robinhood's electronic financial products. Your analytical skills will be key in mitigating money movement risks and safeguarding customer and firm assets. This is an exciting opportunity to help build our brokerage infrastructure and grow your career with us! This role is based in our Denver, CO or Westlake, TX office , with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week (Wednesday, Thursday and Friday). At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Process high-priority transactions, including wires, checks, journals, and bank-linking, ensuring accuracy and timely completion. Evaluate and manage money movement risks from both a customer and firm perspective to mitigate financial losses. Collaborate with project and operations teams to test, launch, and scale retail brokerage products and operational systems. We build the ChatGPT brand through integrated campaigns, creator and social programs, partnerships and cultural experiences. We work with local and global teams to make ChatGPT relevant and useful in people’s everyday lives. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a hands-on Integrated Marketing Manager to lead Consumer and Brand campaigns across LATAM. The role is based in São Paulo and works closely with regional and global teams. You’ll lead the work from strategy through production and launch, and build ongoing marketing programs that keep the brand relevant from always on to major campaigns. items.title: Growth GTM Engineer, Revenue Operations
items.location_text: San Francisco, Austin, New York City
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes. We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine. You'll orchestrate enrichment across marketing and product leads. You'll build the scoring models that combine firmographic and technographic fit with demonstrated intent and product behavior. You'll own the routing that sends each lead back to Marketing for nurture or to BDRs and Sales for engagement. And you'll help build the custom internal apps our reps use to research, prioritize and engage prospects. You'll report to the Head of Marketing Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaigns and attribution. You'll write production code, own the data and logic between our warehouse and Salesforce, and measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue. Tech stack: Salesforce | Snowflake | dbt | Python | TypeScript | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | LLM APIs WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious. - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it. - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users. - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products. - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own enrichment orchestration. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party data providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost, so every record is complete, accurate and ready to act on. - Own and iterate on lead and account scoring. Build fit models from firmographic and technographic attributes such as industry, size, region, tech stack, AI maturity and buying-committee coverage. Combine them with intent and behavior signals: web and content engagement, email and campaign engagement from Marketing Operations, third-party intent, event activity, and product usage signals from the Growth team. Calibrate the models against closed-won and closed-lost data, version them, and explain to Sales why a lead scored the way it did. - Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Marketing Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools. - Close the feedback loop. Instrument the funnel from lead creation to MQL, meeting, opportunity and closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then send those insights back into scoring, routing and Marketing programs. Supply the data behind attribution, which the Head of Marketing Operations owns. - Help build custom internal apps for prospect engagement. Ship the tools reps use every day, such as account and prospect research briefs, signal-triggered alerts in Slack and Salesforce, prioritized call and outreach queues, and LLM-powered agents that draft personalized outreach and prepare reps before first touch. Run them like products: talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used. These apps are part of our BDR prospecting toolset, a combination of internal builds and vendor solutions that the Head of Marketing Operations owns or co-owns. Deliver against that roadmap, including integrating vendor tools with Salesforce and our data layer. - Be the technical owner of the lead data layer. Build and maintain the dbt models, reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that connect Snowflake, Salesforce, marketing automation, enrichment providers and engagement tools. Make sure data flows are observable, tested and trusted. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building the Salesforce and warehouse side of its sync. - Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems. Work with the Growth team, using the PLG signals they publish to drive scoring and routing. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In your first 30 days: - Audit the current enrichment coverage, scoring logic, routing rules and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline. In your first 90 days: - Ship an enrichment waterfall with measurable gains in fill rate and accuracy. - Ship an evolution of our unified scoring model that combines fit, intent and product signals, with a published rubric Sales trusts. - Ship routing that sends every lead to nurture or sales within an agreed SLA, with dashboards that show speed to lead and conversion by route. In your first 6 months: - Ship at least one rep-facing engagement app or agent with sustained weekly use by BDRs and AEs. - Show a measurable lift in MQL-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion. QUALIFICATIONS - 4+ years in GTM engineering, RevOps or Marketing Ops engineering, growth engineering, or data engineering in a B2B SaaS environment, including at least 2 years building enrichment, scoring or routing systems. - Commercial instinct. You start from a revenue problem, like "inbound enterprise leads wait too long for a first touch," and work back to the data, logic or tool that fixes it. - Strong SQL and experience building data models in a warehouse (Snowflake, dbt or similar). You pull your own data. - Production code in Python or TypeScript. You've shipped internal tools, integrations or agents that real users depend on. - Deep working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns, ownership), and experience automating within it and integrating with it. - Hands-on experience with enrichment and intent providers and orchestration tools, such as Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit, 6sense, Demandbase or Common Room. - Fluency with funnel mechanics: lead lifecycle design, scoring models, routing and assignment logic, SLAs, attribution data and conversion metrics. - Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, rate limits and error handling across third-party GTM tools. - Operator and business partner mindset. You work directly with reps and marketers, ship fixes quickly, and don't need a PM to translate requests. NICE TO HAVE - Experience in a hybrid PLG and sales-led motion: product-qualified leads, mapping users to accounts, and sales-assist routing. - Experience with routing and scheduling tools (Default, Chili Piper, LeanData) and reverse ETL (Hightouch, Census, Polytomic). - Experience building LLM-powered research, personalization or qualification agents, including evaluation and monitoring. - Experience with statistical or ML-based scoring (logistic regression, gradient boosting) and model calibration. - Entity resolution and domain-matching experience at scale. - Prior GTM Engineer experience at a GTM-tooling or AI-native company.

items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem to accelerate customer success, enable responsible enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers. Global systems integrators and technology services partners help enterprises move from AI strategy to production deployment. This role will lead OpenAI’s co-sell initiatives with IBM across North America, bringing together IBM’s consulting, technology, industry, and delivery capabilities with OpenAI’s products and platform. You will turn the global partnership strategy into a focused North America sales plan and repeatable field execution that delivers customer and commercial impact. About the Role We are hiring a Partner Sales Director to own IBM’s North America co-sell execution and measurable contribution to OpenAI growth. You will translate the global IBM partnership strategy into a prioritized regional business plan, activate IBM and OpenAI account teams, and drive qualified pipeline, closed business and sustained production adoption in partnership with sales, technical and delivery leaders. The role owns North America account prioritization, field activation, pursuit orchestration and partner forecasting within the global plan. Global partnership strategy, cross-region programs and commercial frameworks remain with global leadership; customer account ownership remains with the relevant OpenAI sales teams. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will connect senior executive engagement with joint account planning, co-selling, solution and delivery alignment, field enablement, governance, and day-to-day execution. Success requires a strong understanding of how a large, matrixed services and technology organization operates, commercial discipline, technical fluency, and the ability to align teams without formal authority. The ideal candidate has led a high-impact partnership with IBM, built measurable pipeline and customer outcomes across North America, and knows how to turn partnership GTM strategy into account-level execution and successful deployments. In this role, you will: - Own North America partner sales and GTM with IBM, including regional strategy, executive alignment, joint planning, pipeline growth, customer outcomes, delivery-readiness coordination and escalation, and long-term expansion, in alignment with the global alliance. - Develop and execute a North America joint business plan with clear account and industry priorities, investments, decision rights, milestones, and measures of success. - Build trusted relationships across IBM Consulting, IBM Technology, North America industry and regional leadership, alliance teams, client account leaders, sales organizations, architects, and delivery leaders, while staying aligned with global stakeholders. - Translate executive priorities into repeatable field execution spanning account mapping, opportunity qualification, co-selling, solution development, technical engagement, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Shape joint solutions and industry plays that combine OpenAI capabilities with IBM’s consulting, technology, hybrid cloud, data, security, governance, and delivery strengths. - Lead joint account planning and strategic customer pursuits with IBM and OpenAI field teams across North America, with particular focus on complex and regulated enterprises. - Create a clear engagement model for OpenAI sellers and technical teams, including when to involve IBM, how opportunities are qualified, who owns each step, and how channel conflict is resolved. - Partner with Product, Engineering, Solutions, Security, Legal, Finance, and Commercial teams to support complex customer engagements and remove technical, contractual, compliance, and operational blockers. - Build IBM’s North America field and delivery readiness through executive sponsorship, sales enablement, technical training, reusable solution patterns, and disciplined delivery handoffs. - Establish regional governance across executive business reviews, pipeline inspection, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation, connected to the global alliance operating model. - Own and track agreed North America commercial targets across qualified partner-sourced and co-sell pipeline, conversion to closed business, OpenAI revenue or consumption, and production adoption, with clear attribution and no double counting. - Align resource priorities with OpenAI sales and technical leaders for North America opportunities with the greatest strategic value, commercial potential, customer impact, delivery readiness, and repeatability. - Represent OpenAI in senior partner, customer, and industry engagements with clarity, sound judgment, and strong executive presence. - Build the regional operating model and identify the team capacity needed to scale the IBM partnership across North America. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Significant experience leading strategic alliances, GSI, or advisory partnerships, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise go-to-market programs in AI, cloud, data, SaaS, or enterprise technology. - Direct experience working with IBM and deep familiarity with its North America organization, consulting and technology businesses, incentives, decision-making networks, commercial model, and enterprise delivery motions. - A proven record of turning a strategic partnership into a qualified pipeline, closed business and production adoption, with clear evidence of your contribution to the commercial results. - Experience designing and scaling joint operating models across large, matrixed organizations, including governance, account planning, incentives, staffing, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Demonstrated success shaping and advancing complex C-suite enterprise transformation opportunities from strategy through production deployment. - Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility with senior IBM and customer leaders while remaining close to operating details. - Commercial judgment and experience prioritizing investments, qualifying opportunities, managing forecasts, and making clear tradeoffs. - Technical fluency across enterprise AI, cloud and hybrid environments, data platforms, integration, security, governance, risk, and modern application architectures. - Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to align Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, and Operations without direct authority. - Experience building partner enablement, joint solutions, industry plays, and scalable field engagement models across North America. - Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure, accountability, and momentum in a rapidly evolving market. - Excellent written and verbal communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills. - A builder mindset, high ownership, low ego, and a consistent focus on customer value and responsible AI adoption. What success looks like - OpenAI and IBM have a clear North America growth strategy, differentiated joint value proposition, executive governance model, and measurable business plan aligned with the global alliance. - IBM and OpenAI field teams across North America know when and how to engage one another, and qualified opportunities progress through a consistent co-sell and delivery motion. - The North America partnership generates qualified pipeline and converts priority opportunities into secure, successful production deployments with demonstrable customer value. - Joint solution patterns and industry plays become repeatable rather than remaining bespoke. - OpenAI resources are allocated transparently toward the highest-impact opportunities. - IBM’s North America teams demonstrate growing readiness and accountability across selling, architecture, implementation, and customer success. - The North America partnership earns sustained executive sponsorship and delivers measurable year-over-year growth. items.title: Lead Product Designer, Growth (Mobile)
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We’ve scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action. ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity is looking for an experienced Lead Product Designer to own mobile design for Growth. You'll shape the experiences that bring Perplexity to as many people as possible on the device they reach for first, making software that feels like the future but can be understood and used by anyone in the world today. Growth design has its own craft and nuance, and so does mobile. You'll own the highest-leverage moments in the mobile user journey: first-run onboarding and activation, consumer acquisition surfaces, conversion flows, paywalls and pricing, the nudges and upsells that drive adoption of new products and features, and the retention loops that turn first-time users into daily ones. This is design where a few pixels, a single step, or the timing of a transition can move real numbers, so you'll pair a high craft bar with rigorous experimentation, letting real data guide the work. You'll do that in the real material: prototyping on device, writing SwiftUI in Xcode, and putting up your own PRs. You care about clarity, craft, details, and delight as much as you care about growth and impact. This role is deeply cross-functional: you'll partner closely with our Growth, Product Marketing, mobile engineering, and brand design teams, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead mobile product design for Growth across the full lifecycle: acquisition, activation, retention, monetization, and enterprise expansion - Design first-run and onboarding experiences that feel native to the platform and get users to value as fast as possible - Craft conversion and upsell flows for mobile, including paywalls, pricing, and plan comparison - Design growth experiences for an AI-native product, getting people to their first great answer fast and helping them discover new capabilities like Computer - Bring the Perplexity brand to life in our growth surfaces through cinematic motion, visual design, and interaction detail - Prototype on device early and often, using real code to answer questions static mocks can't - Write SwiftUI and put up your own PRs, working alongside mobile engineers to close the gap between the design and what ships - Partner closely with Growth and Product Marketing on positioning, messaging, and funnel strategy - Design and run experiments, using data and real usage to drive decisions and measure impact - Explore what new platform capabilities and form factors make possible for growth - Think about how to go from 0→1 but also how to make your decisions scale well - Contribute to process so we're always shipping changes you're proud of, as often as possible WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Experience designing consumer or prosumer products, with a strong track record of shipping native mobile apps - Deep fluency in iOS: platform conventions, navigation patterns, gestures, system components, and what's new each year - A solid understanding of growth nuances: onboarding, activation, acquisition, conversion, upsells, paywalls, pricing, and retention - A data-informed approach, fluent in experimentation, funnels, and metrics, and comfortable learning from usage - Excellent visual, UI, interaction, and motion skills, with a knack for bringing a brand to life in product without getting in the way of use - Comfort prototyping on device, working in Xcode with SwiftUI, and putting up your own PRs in a production codebase - An excellent communicator who can tell a clear story from data and design rationale to team members and leadership - You care about shipping great software more than anything else - Comfort with a high level of autonomy and ambiguity, and the craft to be seen as a peer lead by the rest of the design team - 5+ years of industry experience NICE TO HAVE - Experience designing for Android or working in Jetpack Compose (we design iOS-first, but Android is in scope) - Fluency with motion tools such as Rive, Lottie, or After Effects - You've already been exploring or prototyping interactions for foldables like iPhone Duo NOTES FOR CANDIDATES - Please submit your portfolio with your application.

items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs) - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management. - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production QUALIFICATIONS - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred). - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions. - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments PREFERRED SKILLS - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques - items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Legal team helps Robinhood build and launch products while meeting the rules that apply to a regulated financial company. Our attorneys work alongside Product, Engineering, Compliance and business leaders, giving clear, practical advice on questions that range from new product launches to regulatory matters. We value sound judgment, plain-spoken advice, and a bias toward helping the business move forward the right way. Robinhood is looking for an Assistant General Counsel to join our growing Regulatory legal team. We are looking for an attorney with experience in prediction markets, futures, securities and futures commission merchant/broker-dealer regulatory issues who is excited to work at the intersection of regulation, technology, and finance. We are looking for a highly adaptable and collaborative person who can handle ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities with flexibility and patience. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing company and contribute to our mission to democratize finance for all. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NYC and Washington, DC offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Navigate complex regulatory frameworks to help the business design innovative financial products and services Identify and draft necessary changes to the firm's systems and procedures to meet the requirements of new rules/regulations Engage with regulators, including CFTC, SEC, NFA and FINRA, and other external parties Draft agreements, policies and procedures, disclosures, account documentation and website materials Resolve account issues related to estates, bankruptcies, powers of attorney, and related matters Monitoring CFTC/NFA, SEC/FINRA and SRO rule developments and making resulting recommendations Research prediction market, futures, securities, and brokerage questions and provide legal analysis and recommendations Partner cross-functionally with teams including litigation, compliance, product, and government affairs What you bring J.D. degree (or foreign equivalent) and membership in at least 1 U.S. state bar 7+ years of legal practice, including in-house experience, specializing in CFTC and/or SEC regulatory law Knowledge or expertise in the rules and regulations relevant to futures commission merchants and/or broker-dealers Track record of developing practical solutions to novel problems Exceptional project management and communication skills Experience at a federal or state financial regulatory agency Experience with technology or start-up organizations, and interest in prediction markets What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. items.title: Partner Support Operations Lead
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role The Claude Partner Network is how partners build, sell, and deliver on Claude. Partner Support keeps them moving: getting set up, getting certified, registering their work, and understanding where they stand in the program. It runs in layers. Self-serve and an AI support agent handle what they can, an outsourced vendor team works the in-scope (L1) topics, and our specialists take the escalated (L2) cases that need judgment. As our Partner Support Operations Lead, you will run partner support end to end: the team, the operating model, and the systems behind every layer. Partner Programs sets program policy. You will build and run the service levels, knowledge, quality bar, and escalation paths that put that policy into practice, and keep them reliable as volume grows. This is a hands-on operator and builder role. You will be close enough to the queue to know why a case was hard or a rule broke, while you build the team, the vendor coverage, and the Claude-powered automation that keep support from growing in line with partner count. Key responsibilities Manage the partner support team: set priorities and clear expectations, coach the Partner Support Specialists, address performance early, and expand the team if volume or coverage calls for it Own the support operating model: the L1 and L2 boundary, severity definitions, service levels, and escalation paths; review misrouted and wrongly escalated tickets, and fix the rule as well as the ticket Run the L2 queue to its service levels: coverage across shifts, one owner for every case, clean handoffs to the teams that hold the answer, and careful handling of sensitive and high-impact partner issues Manage the support service line with our business process outsourcing (BPO) team: work with their leads day to day and hold a stated quality bar through training and sign-off for each new cohort, the QA rubric and calibration, the weekly operating review, and corrective action when quality or coverage slips Own the knowledge layer: one source of truth for the help center, macros, and AI agent content, updated when a program change ships, so every layer gives partners the same answer from day one of a launch Own the support platform: routing, conversation attributes, views, workflows, access, and service-level reporting; keep the taxonomy short, consistent, and reportable Scale through self-serve, vendors, and Claude: use topic and outcome data to decide what moves to each, and build automations for tagging, routing, QA screening, and reporting; test them on real tickets and add human checkpoints where a wrong answer carries risk Turn what partners ask into fixes: bring the recurring causes behind ticket volume to Partner Programs, Partner Business Systems, and other owners, and follow each one through until the tickets stop Run support on a scorecard covering responsiveness, resolution, escalation accuracy, and quality, and use it to plan capacity and to tell the team, the vendor, and leadership what to fix next Minimum qualifications Support operations experience at a technology company, including managing a small team Experience running an outsourced or BPO support team: onboarding waves, service levels, QA rubrics, calibration, and performance feedback A track record of building a tiered support model from an early stage and running it as volume grew Hands-on depth in Intercom or a comparable platform (Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud): routing rules, attributes, workflows, reporting, and permissions Experience running knowledge and content for an AI support agent, including how to review answer quality and close content gaps Strong analytical instincts: able to read ticket data, find the cause behind a spike or a backlog, and turn it into a fix and a capacity plan Sound judgment while the program is still moving: able to make the call with incomplete information, hold a policy line with a frustrated partner or an internal stakeholder, and keep the relationship intact A builder's mindset and clear writing: you use tools like Claude to automate your own work, and you document what you build so a new teammate or vendor lead can run it Preferred qualifications Support operations experience in a B2B, partner, or channel environment Experience supporting a partner, reseller, systems integrator, or independent software vendor (ISV) program Experience building support coverage across regions, time zones, or languages Familiarity with Salesforce, and with the Claude API, Claude Code, or MCP The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $215,000 — $300,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
